THE CONTINUOUS EMISSIONS MONITORING SYSTEM IN PLACE FOR SO2 EMISSIONS HAS NOT YET BEEN CERTIFIED AND WORK IS ON-GOING TO RESOLVE POTENTIAL DATA QUALITY ISSUES. properties.title: NRC Report: Sodium Hydroxide (In Black Liquor Sludge) near Groveton, NH
properties.summary: Incident Type: STORAGE TANK - NRC Report ID: 861203 - Medium Affected: OTHER - Suspected Responsible Party: ALLIED RECYCLING, INC.
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 861203
Incident Time: 2008-01-27 05:00:00
Nearest City: Groveton, NH
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: SODIUM HYDROXIDE (IN BLACK LIQUOR SLUDGE)
Medium Affected: OTHER
Suspected Responsible Party: ALLIED RECYCLING, INC.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 100 gallons
CATERPILLAR IS SENIOR SECURED CREDITOR OF GROVETON PAPER BOARD, BANKRUPT OWNER OF PROPERTY ON WHICH SPILL OCCURRED. CATERPILLAR, AS SECURED CREDITOR, SOLD A TANK TO SUSPECTED RESPONSIBLE PARTY, ALLIED RECYCLING, INC. TANK IS LOCATED INSIDE AN INDUSTRIAL BUILDING. ALLIED PURCHASED AND BEGAN DEMOLISHING TANK FOR SCRAP. DURING TANK DEMOLITION, SLUDGE IN TANK WAS RELEASED ONTO BUILDING FLOOR. SLUDGE IS BELIEVED TO BE BLACK LIQUOR, AQUEOUS SOLUTION TYPICALLY COMPOSED OF LIGNIN RESIDUES, HEMICELLULOSE, SODIUM SULFIDE, AND SODIUM HYDROXIDE. MATERIAL IS TYPICALLY HIGH PH DUE TO PRESENCE OF SODIUM HYDROXIDE. FIELD TESTING INDICATED PH IN RANGE OF 10-12. WATER FROM PARTIALLY DEMOLISHED ROOF DRAIN ENTERED SPILL ROOM, MIXED WITH SLUDGE, AND FLOWED OUT OF ROOM INTO NEARBY DRAINAGE SYSTEM. FROM DRAINAGE SYSTEM, DISCHARGED INTO INDUSTRIAL WASTE WATER TREATMENT PLANT OPERATED BY WAUSAU PAPER. WAUSAU DETECTED HIGHER THAN NORMAL PH IN WASTE WATER IN PRIMARY CLARIFIER AND NOTIFIED CATERPILLAR'S AGENT OF APPARENT RELEASE. IT'S NATURE OF THE MATERIAL IS NOT FULLY KNOWN AT THIS POINT (LABORATORY SAMPLES COLLECTED FOR ANALYSIS); MASS OF MATERIAL RELEASED IS NOT KNOWN. HOWEVER, IT IS POSSIBLE THAT MASS O MATERIAL RELEASED EXCEEDED THE RQ FOR NAOH. WAUSAU REPORTED THAT HIGH PH WATER WAS TREATED AND DID NOT ENTER WATERS RECEIVING TREATMENT PLANT DISCHARGE.
